summary.text: Brad Schneider is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to Illinois's 10th District. A former business consultant and life insurance agency owner, he was first elected in 2012, lost in 2014, and won the seat back in 2016. He sits on the House Ways and Means and Foreign Affairs committees, chairs the New Democrat Coalition, and won his March 2026 primary against Morgan Coghill.

paragraphs.text: Schneider was born in Denver, Colorado, in 1961 and graduated from Cherry Creek High School there.
He earned a bachelor's degree in industrial engineering from Northwestern University in 1983 and an MBA from Northwestern's Kellogg School of Management.
After working on a kibbutz in Israel for a year, he returned to the Chicago area to work at PriceWaterhouseCoopers.

According to his official biography, Schneider's business career spanned nearly three decades, principally as a business advisor helping company leaders plan strategic growth, and he also owned and managed a life insurance agency.
Wikipedia lists him as managing principal of Davis Dann Adler Schneider, LLC (1997-2003), at Blackman Kallick, and founder of Cadence Consulting Group in 2008.

Schneider won the 2012 Democratic primary and then defeated Republican incumbent Bob Dold in the general election, 51%-49%. He lost the 2014 rematch to Dold, then defeated him in 2016, 53%-47%, after winning the Democratic primary over Highland Park Mayor Nancy Rotering.
He has represented Illinois's 10th District in Congress since 2017, after also serving one term from 2013 to 2015, and his official biography says he was re-elected in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024.

Schneider serves on the House Ways and Means and Foreign Affairs committees and previously served on Judiciary and Small Business. His official biography cites work on international tax, health care innovation, sustainable aviation fuel and repeal of the SALT deduction cap.
He is a co-founder and co-chair of the bipartisan Abraham Accords Caucus, chair of the New Democrat Coalition since 2025, and vice-chair of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force.
According to his official biography, Schneider and his wife, Julie, have lived in the district for more than 30 years, raised two sons, and now live in Highland Park.
